# SmartMetadataMatcher — v0.5.38 Draft Bridge Integration

**Status:** Source-only integration candidate, not a release or proof of Playnite behavior. Generated by the guarded v0.5.38 builder. No changes to the existing metadata writer, journal schemas, ROM files, launch actions or Playnite game data during the build.

## Delivered in this milestone

- **Native Design C draft transfer:** Checked and current session drafts are copied into the existing `CatalogWindow` draft store when the user proceeds to Classic from a marked Design C batch. Import still requires Classic's independent identity checks, proposed titles and fields review, verified-backup acknowledgment and final approval. No second writer.
- **Fail-closed draft binding:** A transferred draft is required for its game. If Playnite title/platform or IGDB ID/title changed, the imported draft will not quietly fall back to all default metadata fields. The user must review again; **Reset draft** is an explicit intentional exception.
- **Title-cleanup guard repair:** The old SmartAuto block that demanded unchecking a now-hidden checkbox is removed. Safely reviewed exact/confirmed candidates may clean Playnite display titles. Smart-inferred automatic candidates are conservatively kept under their existing Playnite title unless the identity is explicitly confirmed. They may still fill missing metadata under the existing writer/identity checks. This policy prevents an unconfirmed inferred match from changing edition-sensitive titles.
- **Per-game approved title policy:** The batch's displayed `PlannedTitle` is bound to the per-item `RenameRequested` passed to the existing `CatalogEnrichmentWriter.ApplyOne`; the writer still rejects a title that differs from approval.
- **Batch-wide native title reservation:** The Design C read-only marked preview considers earlier proposed titles in the same selected batch, using existing `CatalogImportDraft.ResolveTitle` rather than a duplicate naming algorithm.
- **Regression coverage:** Expanded native C# batch tests and a static source invariant suite. The builder runs existing source safety scripts, Windows .NET build and all offline C# tests before applying local source.

## Not yet implemented / still to do

This milestone is **not** full single-window functionality. Design C still uses Classic for identity review, the final approval dialog, live IGDB preflight, application, journaling, undo and recovery. Strict automatic freshness remains `false` when shown from a saved candidate in the native preview. That is intentional: scores from saved scans must never become proof of current strict identity. A new shared live-evidence and exact-fields coordinator remains the next milestone, followed by direct Design C approve/apply and remaining advanced feature parity.

The native preview still offers a preliminary field estimate, not a predownloaded exact live media plan. The Classic final list also shows potential fields, so no claim is made that final exact-field planning is finished.

Drafts not selected in the batch are not persisted across closing the Design C window. The selected transferred draft is preserved for the Classic final approved plan; a cancelled review may still require reopening and re-entering a draft. Persistent/native state becomes part of the direct single-workspace milestone.

## Verification gates

1. `py -3 <builder.zip> --self-test`: package payload/inventory check on any Python 3 machine.
2. `py -3 <builder.zip> --project <local repo> --check-only`: exact v0.5.37 input UI/planner/test hashes and source anchors. Read-only.
3. `py -3 <builder.zip> --project <local repo> --apply`: isolated Windows build + static source checks + existing .NET unit tests + package checks; verified byte-exact source backup; **then** guarded local source apply. No installation/commit/push.
4. Manual Playnite 10 test: staged custom title/description and missing-field opt-out passed to Classic final review; cancel causes no write; on explicit approval writer honors the draft; undo restores all plugin-changed fields.
5. Manual negative cases: edit Playnite name or platform after staging; change IGDB edition; duplicate custom title; same-batch repeated canonical titles; smart-inferred automatic result; canceled network request; blocked recovery journal. No writes on a failed preflight.

**Source backup is not a Playnite library backup.** Preserve existing Playnite database and extension-data backups before any actual metadata import test. The installer does not perform such a test or a Playnite installation.

## Next implementation return point

Extract a shared typed read-only live IGDB identity + Playnite snapshot + exact field/preview coordinator from `CatalogWindow.RunBatch`, then make Design C own the final approval UI and call the existing unchanged journaled writer. Maintain the launch-guard dispositions from the November 11, 2026 final audit. Do not reintroduce temporary 25/5-game UI caps as product defaults, but preserve identity/edition checks, bounded resources and recovery integrity.
